Which role does what?

The #1 question, answered

02 · Orchestrator

Advises + builds agents

Your single entry point. Like a chief of staff: it figures out how work should get done, then makes it happen.

  • Picks Autonomous, Conversational, or Hybrid mode
  • Routes “what & whether” to Consulting, “do it” to Execution
  • Prepares your approval packages & briefings
“How should this get done, by whom, and in which mode?”
✓ Builds agents
03 · Consulting Organization

Advises only

A 34-role advisory team in 7 practices (A–G). Expertise areas — not separate agents. It reports back; it never executes.

  • Discovery, feasibility & viability rating
  • Mandatory legal & regulatory gate report
  • Market, CFO, tax, formation & design playbooks
“What should be done — and is it viable?”
Never builds agents
04 · Execution Organization

Builds + runs agents

A CEO plus 19 specialist agents that carry out approved work only — tracked, reviewed, and verified before anything closes.

  • One accountable owner per task
  • Independent quality review & stop-work rules
  • Daily, weekly & gate reporting
“Is the approved work actually done — and verified?”
✓ Builds agents

All three share one rulebook: 01 Core Charter (authority order, integrity rules, gates, evidence labels) and 05 Appendix templates T1–T12. The 06 Compact edition squeezes it all into ~6,300 characters for tight instruction limits.

8 stages, 7 gates

You pass every gate

Hard rule (C7.1): no material or irreversible spending until the legal and regulatory prerequisites are researched — agencies, exact forms, fees, sequence, timeline, and what’s still uncertain. That’s why Gate G2 is highlighted. Every gate review ends in Go, Conditional-Go, Pivot, or No-Go — and you decide.

Who does what

Charter C5

🤖 AI does

  • Research & analysis
  • Calculations & financial models
  • Drafting, planning, documentation
  • Diagrams & task tracking
  • Quality review
  • Preparing forms & approval packages

👤 You do (founder only)

  • Strategic choices & gate decisions
  • Signatures & payments
  • Identity verification & physical attendance
  • Final submissions & certifications
  • Relationship building

🤝 Together

  • Business strategy
  • Financial assumptions
  • Operating model design
  • License applications
  • Implementation & expansion planning

⚠️ Always needs your approval first

  • Spending, debt, leases, equipment
  • Contracts & paid agreements
  • Forming or changing an entity
  • Hiring or firing
  • Legal filings & certifications
  • Passing a gate or launching

One objective, start to finish

Illustrated in the pack with a Columbus vending business (traditional snacks & beverages) — example only, not researched facts.

  1. You define the objective.
  2. Orchestrator checks capabilities, picks a mode, splits the work.
  3. Consulting researches feasibility — market, money, legal.
  4. Orchestrator brings you an approval package. You decide.
  5. Execution creates tasks, one owner each.
  6. Work is executed, reviewed, and verified.
  7. Knowledge base is updated — tasks, evidence, logs.
  8. You get an executive briefing.
  9. You do the founder-only actions (sign, pay, file).
  10. Orchestrator starts the next cycle.
Before any task with files: the pre-execution protocol (C15) — triage first (names → headers → headings → targeted sections, full text only when required), build a Working Context Brief, then execute. And every file follows the naming pattern (C16): PROJECT_AREA_TYPE-NNN_Title_vX.Y_STATUS_DATE — e.g. CBUSVEND_LEG_PLN-003_Vendor-License-Plan_v1.2_APPROVED_20261119.md.
Source: your AI Business Organization Prompt Pack (00_README through 06_COMPACT + architecture.json). Diagrams are the pack’s own renders, shown full-size in the viewer. Evidence labels used across the system: VERIFIED · OFFICIAL · ESTIMATE · ASSUMPTION · RECOMMENDATION · UNVERIFIED · NEEDS_PRO_REVIEW.
